chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father, altogether from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:
Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) judged regarding a slave who stole and betrayed from the wealth of his master. He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no cutting upon him.'

key_terms.قَطْعٌ: Cutting (referring to the hadd of amputation for theft)

ai.seo_question: What is the hadd penalty for a slave who steals from his master?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Baqir (AS) clarifies that the fixed hadd punishment of amputation (qat') for theft does not apply to slaves, reflecting the Shia juristic view that slaves are subject to a different penal structure due to their status. It highlights the distinction between the master's right to discipline and the divine hadd, a key topic in al-Kulayni’s chapter on the legal status of owned and contracted slaves.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad and Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, altogether from Abdul Rahman Bin Abu Najran, from Aasim Bin Humeyd, from Muhammad Bin Qays, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>
having said: ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> judged regarding a slave who stole and betrayed from the wealth of his master. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no cutting upon him’.
